findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached FLOWR endpoint VJP, so coordinate contrasts are not physical interaction energies.

The observed learning window is [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score times at 0.01 spacing, and recorded affinities were removed under an equal score prior, so no decoded terminal affinity labels are available for the current study.

Continuous contrast features over the observed support are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass shows 4 sign changes with first_rate_z positive and last_rate_z negative, and landmark_00_local_dx shows 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts, so a constant rule is not supported and any time-conditioned rule must stay within observed-node interpolation.

Several landmark local-derivative features have large-magnitude first and last rate z-scores with opposite signs (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z strongly negative, last_rate_z positive; landmark_00_local_cyy similar), indicating rate turnover rather than a stable directional drift.

Polynomial fits are not accepted for these continuous features and extrapolation is disallowed, so the evidence supports only observed-node interpolation and cannot be extended beyond the observed window.

hypotheses.falsifier: a constant rule matching observed-node contrasts within the reported node RMSE, or sign changes not reproducible at observed nodes
hypotheses.observable: sign and magnitude of landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_d* contrasts at observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast rule that follows the observed sign of landmark soft-mass and local-derivative contrasts at observed score nodes would track the observed non-monotone pattern better than a constant rule, without extrapolating beyond the observed window.

hypotheses.falsifier: consistent same-sign rates across the window with accepted polynomial fit
hypotheses.observable: first_rate_z versus last_rate_z sign disagreement per feature
hypotheses.statement: Rate turnover in landmark local-derivative contrasts reflects within-window change in the coordinate contrast rather than a stable cohort-level direction, so any reward recipe expressing it must remain a coordinate contrast and not a velocity target.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Only continuous_trends rows were read; branch_adjusted, survival_effects, increment_effects, turnover_accounting, joint_diagnostics and regional_effects were not inspected, so multiplicity-adjusted ranking, joint coupling and turnover accounting comparisons remain unassessed.
No validated contrast function curve was retrieved via get_curve, so fit fidelity beyond the reported relative_node_RMSE and sign-change counts is not established.
The evidence is diagnostic coordinate contrast only; it is not physical interaction energy and does not establish neural-module causation.
